newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent slips in correction to Wednesday's rise.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent slips in correction to Wednesday's rise.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were weaker on Thursday morning after OPEC oil ministers in Vienna agreed at talks on Wednesday to freeze current output quotas until the end of the year.
August Brent was seven cents a barrel lower at $18.15 at 0957 GMT, after a hefty 34-cent gain on Wednesday following the OPEC news. Gas oil was $2.25 a tonne firmer at $162.50.
"There is no real new reason this morning," one broker at the IPE said. "There was a good move up yesterday and this is a little retracement in response to that."
"We are still above $18.00 and that is a good sign."
GNI Ltd said in a daily research report: "The OPEC result was pretty much within expectations."

The accord that is being extended sets a ceiling on total volume by the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries at 25.03 million barrels daily, including volume from Iraq under its food-for-oil deal with the United Nations.
Announcing Wednesday's decision, OPEC Secretary-General Rilwanu Lukman said that all 11 cartel members gave individual pledges that they would now adhere to mandatory limits.
Lukman said no threats had been made against alleged violators but that they had made promises to colleagues and OPEC believed them.
Venezuela's oil minister Erwin Arrieta on Thursday denied reports that his country was overproducing.
But worries persist about continued overproduction by Venezuela and other OPEC members.
"Few, if any, of the oil ministers concerned have made supportive comments so far and clearly it will be impossible to police any continuing overproduction," GNI said.

"As the saying goes, 'the proof of the pudding is in the eating', and the market will simply have to wait for the next couple of monthly production estimates to see how prices are likely to map out into the fourth quarter (of the year.)"
